ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the left side of the figure is a schematic map of South America, and the right side is an enlarged map of Chile and its surroundings; the legend on the right marks area A and area B. Area A is distributed in a long and narrow belt along the west coast of South America and near the Andes Mountains, and area B is also only a local black narrow patch distribution; neither of the two is a large continuous plain. Then reason: after identifying areas A and B according to the legend and comparing their area and form, it can be seen that both have relatively narrow and localized distribution ranges, so the scale of land that can be used for cultivation is commonly shown as relatively small.
